newsitem.title: USA: S. Calif. home sales rose 5.2 pct in Feb - report.
newsitem.headline: S. Calif. home sales rose 5.2 pct in Feb - report.

text.p: Southern California home sales in February jumped by more than five percent from the same month last year, according to a report on Thursday.

A total of 14,442 new and resale houses and condominiums were sold in Los Angeles, Ventura, Orange, San Diego, Riverside and San Bernardino counties last month, according to a report by DataQuick Information Systems.
The sales rate was up 1.1 percent from 14,278 in January and up 5.2 percent from 13,726 for February last year.

The sales count was the strongest for any February since 1990, when 17,861 homes were sold, the report said. Southland sales counts have now increased on a year-over-year basis for the last fifteen months in a row, it said.

"The market is strong, but certainly not overheating like we saw in the late '80s. Prices are still showing the early signs of a modest come-back," Mike Ela, DataQuick's president, said in a statement.
The median price paid for a southern California home was $160,000 in February, unchanged from January and up 1.3 percent from $158,000 for February a year ago, DataQuick said.
DataQuick monitors real estate activity nationwide.
